description: Fork of exp726 (E=384, NAP-bump, hybrid_smooth_autograd, hybrid_smooth_n_alt=NAP=full Hamming-1 ball, save_memory, = 1.1997 @ 276.83M). Single change: hybrid_smooth_n_alt 'NAP' (per-module = full ball) -> '1' (top-2: main + Hamming-1 alt at least-confident bit). Forward gathers only 2 rows per table; backward (autograd) is self-consistent over those same 2 rows. Should be ~3-4x cheaper than exp726's (NAP+1)-row forward, and identical-to-exp724 forward shape (2 rows). Tests: does the n_alt=1 + autograd path match exp724's 1.1936 (K-row soft surrogate backward over 2-row forward) at lower FLOPs? Reference points: exp724=1.1936 (K-row backward, n_alt=1 forward); exp726=1.1997 (sparse backward, n_alt=NAP forward).
